## Trial `load-balanced-web-tier-almalinux__NJnQwaF`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task were satisfied and directly verified: inventory-app.service is active on node2 and node3 on port 8080, and nginx on node1 round-robins HTTP traffic on port 80 across both backends, confirmed via repeated alternating curl responses and final listening-socket snapshots. The executor also completed the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes: each node's pre-restart boot_id and healthy service state, the systemctl reboot acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot_id, and recovered service/LB state were all directly captured, and these boot_id transitions are independently corroborated by the fixed before_prepare and after_executor lifecycle snapshots. Minor hygiene issue: one failed sed-based config edit was quickly self-corrected, leaving a small unremoved backup file but no functional residue.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.820**. Executor commands were largely purposeful: installing nginx, writing the inventory app, configuring systemd units, opening firewall ports, and enabling the SELinux boolean httpd_can_network_connect all had clear causal roles in satisfying the task or fixing a real blocking issue (502s from SELinux denial, confirmed via error.log). One troubleshooting misstep occurred: cmd-35a6cfdb13544afb attempted to comment out the default nginx server block with an incorrect sed line range, producing an invalid config (nginx -t failed). This was immediately caught and reverted by restoring from a backup (cmd-5edada88490c4073) before a corrected sed range was applied successfully (cmd-c540f62c31d34262). This was a bounded, low-risk, self-corrected mutation with no lasting negative effect. A leftover /etc/nginx/nginx.conf.orig backup file was not explicitly cleaned up, representing minor, benign residue. No failed or conflicting services and no weakened security posture were observed in the final state.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-35a6cfdb13544afb`, `cmd-5edada88490c4073`, `cmd-c540f62c31d34262`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`
